There exist absolute constants $C,c\ge1$ and one randomized multitape Turing machine $\mathcal A$ with the following property. For every $n\ge2$, every rational $p\in(0,1]$, and every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, given $n,p$ in binary and access to independent ordinary deletion traces of $x$, the machine requests at most $$M_C(n,p)=\left\lceil\exp\bigl(CB(n,p)\bigr)\right\rceil$$ traces, outputs an element of $\{0,1\}^n$, and returns $x$ with probability at least $2/3$.*

*For every internal random-bit sequence and every well-formed trace stream of strings of length at most $n$, it halts within $$\bigl(n+L+M_C(n,p)\bigr)^c$$ bit operations. This bound includes preprocessing, all parameter and finite-precision calculations, every received trace bit and delimiter, and the output. The only oracle operation is the external generation of the independent deletion traces.

outputs.exact_statement: For integer $n\ge 2$ and $0<p\le1$, worst-case trace reconstruction of binary strings is possible in this channel with at most $$\exp\!\left(O\!\left(p^{-1}(\log n)^3(1+\log\log(2n))^6\right)\right)$$ traces, with an absolute constant. Write $q=1-p$. More finely, when $q>0$, setting $\mathcal X=1+\log n/(1+\log(1/q))$, the logarithm of the required sample budget is at most $$O\big(p^{-1}(\log n)\mathcal X^2 (1+\log\mathcal X)^6\big)$$ with an absolute constant. In particular for fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and $0\le q\le n^{-\varepsilon}$ the number of traces can be polynomial in $n$ (with parameters of the polynomial allowed to depend on $\varepsilon$). The same asymptotic bounds also suffice for strings with general symbols (assuming exact observation of retained symbols). This concerns sample complexity, not computational efficiency.
